speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a history of high fever and seizures accompanied by a generalized nonpruritic rash; could you tell me exactly how long these symptoms have been present and what your highest recorded temperature was?

speaker: Patient
text: 9-month-old infant. The patient is brought in due to a generalized nonpruritic rash for 2 days. The rash started on the trunk and spread to the extremities. Five days ago, the patient had a fever of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and experienced a 1-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The infant was born at term, has no history of serious illness, and her immunizations are up to date. The current medication includes acetaminophen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Roseola Infantum (Exanthem Subitum).

The clinical presentation of a high fever followed by a rash appearing as the fever resolves is classic for this condition, likely caused by HHV-6. Given the recent seizure, I recommend requesting a complete blood count (CBC) and C-reactive protein (CRP) to rule out bacterial sepsis or meningitis. REQUEST TEST: CBC, CRP.
